Electronegativity (E.N.) The electronegativity of an element is defined as the relative tendency of an atom in a molecule to attract a shared pair of electron towards itself i.e. ability of an atom to attract the shared pair of the electron. It is expressed in number of scales like Pauling's scale, Mulliken's scale but most commonly used scale is Pauling's scale.
Factor Affecting Electronegativity Following are factors:
1. Atomic size: Smaller the size of an atom higher the value of E.N.
2 Number of inner shells: Atom having larger number of inner shells has the lower value of E.N.
3. Number and nature of atoms bonded to it: E.N. of an element depends upon the number and
nature of the atom to which it is bonded. Example- E-N- of P-atom in PCIs is higher than that in PF5 because F is more E.N. than Cl.
4. Types of hybridization: E.N of an element Increase as the s-character in the hybrid orbital

Increase. The E.N. value of carbon in methane< ehene < ethyne. This is due to methane (sp3 hybridi7ation) = 25% s-character, ethane (sp2 hybridization) = 33% s-character, ethyne (sp hvbrtdization) = 50% s-character.
5. Charge of the ion: Cation is smaller in size as compared to the corresponding atom. As a result,

cation should attract electron more readily than its parent atom. So cation has higher E:N. than its parent atom. Cation having higher positive charge is more electronegative. Since, anion is less E.N. than its parent atom.
6. I.P. and E.A. : If the value of I.P. and E.A. is high , the E.N. value will also be high.
Variation of E.N. in a group: When 'eve move from top to bottom, the size of an atom increase, due to this the value of E.N. decrease.
Variation of E.N. in a period: The value of E.N. increase when we move from left to right in period due to smaller in size and higher nuclear charge.
